question:
A network administrator must perform a system upgrade on a Cisco MDS 9000 Series Switch. Due to the recent changes by the security team:
* The AAA server is unreachable.
* All TCP communication between the MDS 9000 Series Switch and AAA servers is disabled.
Which actions must be used to perform the upgrade?
options: Log in locally to the MDS 9000 Series Switch using a network-admin role and download the upgrade files from the remote TFTP server.
Log in locally to the MDS 9000 Series Switch using a server-admin role and download the upgrade files from the remote FTP server.
Log in to a server storing the upgrade files remotely using a server-admin role and download the files to the MDS 9000 Series Switch using SFTP.
Log in to a server storing the upgrade files remotely using a network-admin role and download the files to the MDS 9000 Series Switch using HTTP.
theory: If the AAA servers are unreachable and TCP to them is blocked, remote authentication cannot succeed, so the engineer must fall back to a local account on the switch itself; NX-OS always keeps local authentication as a fallback method, and a locally-defined 'network-admin' role has the full privileges needed to perform software installs. Because TFTP uses UDP (not the disabled TCP path) to reach the file server, downloading the upgrade images via TFTP after a local login is the only option consistent with both constraints in the scenario. (General Cisco NX-OS AAA/software upgrade practice)
